itemOffered.name: Drug Offences Defence
itemOffered.description: Drug offences cover the possession, supply, production, and importation of controlled drugs. Simple possession is usually dealt with in the Magistrates' Court. Supply, conspiracy, and importation are tried in the Crown Court. Astons Law Chambers acts for defendants in drug allegations — from possession through to supply, importation, and production.

itemOffered.name: Supply, Conspiracy, and Importation Defence

itemOffered.name: Forensic Challenges — Purity, Weight, and Attribution
itemOffered.description: Expert-led challenges to drug forensic evidence — purity, weight, and attribution to the defendant.

mainEntity.name: Will my drug case go to the Crown Court?

acceptedAnswer.text: Simple possession often stays in the Magistrates' Court. Supply, importation, and conspiracy allegations are tried at the Crown Court.

mainEntity.name: Can the forensic evidence in a drug case be challenged?

acceptedAnswer.text: Often, yes. Purity, weight, and attribution to the defendant are all open to challenge. The route depends on the disclosure and what an independent expert says.

mainEntity.name: I have been told to expect a long sentence for a drug offence — is that right?

acceptedAnswer.text: It is too early to know. Sentence depends on the role accepted, the weight, and personal mitigation. The first call covers a realistic view, not a worst-case one.
